newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks fall for third year running.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks fall for third year running.

text.p: Colombian stock prices fell in real terms for the third consecutive year in 1996 amid the economic slump and high interest rates, the Securities Superintendency said Thursday.
Bogota's IBB index increased 11.8 percent in nominal terms, equivalent to a fall of 9.83 percent once the 1996 inflation figure of 21.63 percent, released early Thursday, is factored in.
The IBOMED general price index in Medellin fell 3.12 percent in nominal terms --a real term drop of 24.75 percent -- the Securities Superintendency said in its brief year-end report.
The much smaller Bolsa de Occidente exchange, based in Cali, Colombia's second largest city, gained 15.6 percent in nominal terms, a loss of 6.03 percent in real terms.

At their recent conference, stock brokers blamed the low profitability of Colombian stocks on the concentration of large portfolios in just a few hands, the general economic recession and bank interest rates, which have remained high throughout the year. They saw little prospect of improvement in 1997.
The gross domestic product grew just 3 percent in 1996, one of its lowest rates this decade.
Bank deposit rates, currently averaging about 28 percent, were running at above 30 percent for most of the year.

Securities worth a total of 36.3 trillion pesos were traded in Colombia's three bourses in the year, a 41.2 percent nominal increase compared to 1995. Share trading made up 2.3 trillion, of 6.4 percent of total trading. Certificates of deposit accounted for the biggest proportion, 15.6 trillion pesos or 42.9 percent while private bonds made up 9.1 trillion or 25.1 percent of the annual trade.
